findings.title: getBaseConditions may return an unwrapped top-level OR predicate
findings.body: When only authorization conditions exist, getBaseConditions returns authConditions as-is. For org and team scopes, the generated authorization SQL is a top-level OR expression. If a caller composes this fragment with additional SQL using AND, such as `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND ...`, SQL operator precedence will bind the added condition only to the right-hand OR branch, producing incorrect filtering and potentially bypassing added restrictions. The returned base condition should always be parenthesized as a single boolean expression.

findings.title: Exact SQL array assertions depend on nondeterministic DB ordering
findings.body: The org-scope test compares generated Prisma.sql fragments against exact arrays of team IDs and user IDs. The service builds those arrays from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds without enforcing an ORDER BY or sorting the IDs afterward. PostgreSQL does not guarantee row order without ORDER BY, so these tests can pass or fail nondeterministically. Sort the IDs in the service before constructing the SQL, or assert order-insensitively.

findings.title: Org scope skips member lookup when the org has no child teams
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition only queries memberships when teamsFromOrg.length > 0. However, teamIds always includes options.orgId, and an organization can have direct memberships even if it has no child teams. In that case userIdsFromOrg is forced to an empty array, so the generated condition only matches team bookings and excludes all non-team bookings for org users. The membership lookup should not be gated on the existence of child teams.

findings.title: No integration test executes the org/team ANY(array) authorization conditions
findings.body: The only raw-query integration test exercises a user-scope condition with simple equality filters. The org/team authorization paths, which rely on `teamId = ANY(...)` and `userId = ANY(...)`, are only asserted by structural Prisma.sql equality. If the array binding or generated SQL is invalid at runtime, the current tests will not catch it. Add an integration test that executes an org/team base condition against seeded bookings.
